faqs.q: Groundhogs keep burrowing around my Suffolk home — can they be removed?
faqs.a: Yes. The woodchuck, or groundhog, is a designated nuisance species in Virginia and also counts as a higher-risk rabies species in raccoon-variant areas, so burrows against a foundation, slab, or barn in Suffolk are worth acting on before the tunnel system undermines concrete. Our crew handles groundhogs at the property under permit — Virginia does not allow trap-and-relocate — and advises on fencing and harbor removal so the burrow stays empty.

Suffolk.wildlife_intro:
Suffolk is Virginia's largest city by land area — downtown blocks, villages, farms, and swamp edge in one jurisdiction in Suffolk. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: great Dismal Swamp and Lake Drummond, Nansemond River, peanut-country villages. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Suffolk — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
